name: healthcare
appliesTo: Hospitals, clinics, booking and telemedicine, pharmacy, lab results. Formal in structure, but the reader is frightened, so the words carry more than usual.

address.patient: anh/chị by default. Older patients: cô/chú, bác. Never bạn.
address.clinician: bác sĩ, and address them by role — Bác sĩ + full name.
address.self: phòng khám / bệnh viện / chúng tôi

wrong: bảo hiểm sức khỏe nhà nước
glossary.why: BHYT is the statutory scheme and has one name.
Clinical term patients are given on discharge papers.

extraRules.why: Product copy that interprets a result is practising medicine. A lab value shown with `bình thường` attached becomes a diagnosis the clinician did not give.
extraRules.instead: state the number and the reference range, and route interpretation to the clinician

extraRules.why: Clinical labels applied to a person in interface copy read as a judgement. In a chart they are neutral; on a screen the patient is holding they are not.
extraRules.instead: name the condition in relation to care, not to the person — `đang điều trị …`

notes: Appointment times use the 24-hour clock. Dates day-first. Bad news gets the shortest, plainest sentence available and a named next step — never a softener that buries it. Anything that could be read as advice needs a clinician's sign-off, not a copywriter's.
